stories.title: IndiGo extends suspension of Saudi Arabia flights
stories.summary: IndiGo has extended the suspension of flights to Jeddah and Madinah until November 21, and to Riyadh and Dammam until November 30. The airline cited a careful assessment of safety and security conditions following regional conflict. The carrier is notifying affected customers of the schedule changes.

stories.title: IndiGo and India Post promote postcard writing
stories.summary: IndiGo and the Department of Posts have launched the second edition of their Digital Detox initiative. Passengers on 15 flights across 11 destinations were encouraged to trade digital screens for handwritten postcards. The campaign coincided with the Diwali festive season to promote traditional communication methods.

Under its latest advisory, services to and from Jeddah and Madinah will remain cancelled until November 21, 2026, inclusive, while flights

stories.title: Air India considers former Garuda executive for CFO
stories.summary: Air India is reportedly considering Balagopal Kunduvara for the role of chief financial officer. Kunduvara recently stepped down from Garuda Indonesia after a one-year tenure. The airline is seeking to strengthen its finances following a record annual loss and ongoing operational challenges.

stories.title: GMR proposes distance-based fees at Bhogapuram airport
stories.summary: GMR Airports has proposed a distance-based user development fee structure for its new Bhogapuram airport. The plan would nearly double fees over five years, with costs varying by flight distance. GMR states the charges are necessary to recover investment costs. The proposal has drawn criticism from IndiGo.

stories.title: Indian airlines expand in-house maintenance
stories.summary: IndiGo, Air India, and Akasa Air are building their own maintenance, repair, and overhaul capabilities. Engineering chiefs stated that the domestic aftermarket has failed to keep pace with rapid fleet growth. Reliance on overseas providers is now viewed as an exposure risk for the carriers.

stories.title: Bihar student selected for IndiGo cadet programme
stories.summary: Vanshika Viraj, a 20-year-old from Bihar, has been selected for the IndiGo Cadet Pilot Programme. She was the only candidate from her state to reach the final stage of the selection process. She will now begin training in the Philippines to pursue a commercial pilot career.

stories.title: Air Serbia balances growth and fuel costs
stories.summary: Air Serbia is entering the winter season with a strong balance sheet while managing elevated fuel prices. The airline remains cautiously optimistic about its growth trajectory despite current market uncertainty. The full report on the carrier's operational strategy is available to Aviation Week subscribers.

stories.title: Frontier Airlines introduces first-class seating
stories.summary: Frontier Airlines has opened reservations for its new first-class section, which launches in March 2027. The offering includes the first two rows of each aircraft with no middle seats and 37 inches of seat pitch. Bundles start at $129 one way for the budget carrier.

stories.title: Spirit Airlines revises data sale agreement
stories.summary: Spirit Airlines has revised a $10 million data sale agreement with Google to address union concerns. The updated terms exclude a decade of payroll records, tax forms, and employee timecard data. The original scope of the sale had previously drawn objections from crew unions.

stories.title: Chorus Aviation reports Q3 earnings
stories.summary: Chorus Aviation reported adjusted EBITDA of CAD47.7 million for the third quarter of 2026, down from CAD51.6 million in the same period last year. Adjusted net income remained flat at CAD15.1 million. The company reported a leverage ratio of 1.4 times, within its target range.

stories.title: Alaska Airlines launches invite-only concierge status
stories.summary: Alaska Airlines has introduced Atmos Global Concierge, an invitation-only elite status tier for its most valuable customers. The program offers personalized travel assistance and sits above the existing Titanium level. Invitations were sent to selected members on November 9, with benefits extending through the end of 2027.

stories.title: Aeromexico adds six U.S. routes
stories.summary: Aeromexico plans to launch six nonstop routes from Mexico City to the U.S. and Puerto Rico in 2027. New destinations include Nashville, New Orleans, and San Juan. The expansion follows a court ruling that preserved the airline's joint venture with Delta Air Lines.

stories.title: SAS expands summer 2027 schedule
stories.summary: SAS is increasing flights from Copenhagen to Atlanta and Seattle as part of an extensive expansion of its summer 2027 schedule. The carrier is adding capacity across seven intercontinental routes and 20 European destinations. The expansion follows the airline's transition from Star Alliance to the SkyTeam partnership.

stories.title: Southwest Airlines adds five international routes
stories.summary: Southwest Airlines is launching five new international routes during the Northern Hemisphere winter season. The carrier, which operates the world's largest fleet of Boeing 737 aircraft, began service from Las Vegas to Mexico on November 1. Additional routes are expected to launch early in 2027.

stories.title: American Airlines adds 23 routes from major hubs
stories.summary: American Airlines has added 23 new routes from its three busiest hubs in Dallas, Charlotte, and Chicago. These locations account for 60 percent of the airline's total activity. Daily departures across the trio fluctuate significantly, ranging from 799 on Thanksgiving to 2,121 on November 29.

stories.title: Air Transat cancels Montreal to Athens route
stories.summary: Air Transat has removed its seasonal link between Montreal and Athens from its 2027 schedule. The carrier previously operated three weekly flights using Airbus A330-200 aircraft. Air Canada will continue to serve the route, and Air Transat maintains its existing three-weekly service from Toronto to Athens.

stories.title: American Airlines seeks widebody fleet replacement
stories.summary: American Airlines has issued formal requests for proposals to Boeing and Airbus for a new widebody order. The airline is looking to replace its Boeing 777-200ER fleet, which was previously expected to undergo cabin refurbishments. The carrier currently relies on both manufacturers for its narrowbody aircraft.

stories.title: Archer Aviation price targets lowered by analysts
stories.summary: Needham and Cantor Fitzgerald lowered their price targets for Archer Aviation following third-quarter results. Needham reduced its target to $7 from $9, while Cantor Fitzgerald cut its target to $10 from $11. Shares traded 5 percent lower following the announcement. The company remains in the development phase.

stories.title: Archer Aviation reports third-quarter loss
stories.summary: Archer Aviation reported an adjusted net loss of $274.5 million for the third quarter of 2026, with a loss of $0.35 per share. Shares fell 2.1 percent to $4.71 following the release. The company continues to operate with a high-growth narrative despite ongoing cash burn.

stories.title: Premium Economy On US Airlines: How The Big 3 Actually Compare
stories.summary: Demand for premium air travel is growing as passengers are increasingly prioritizing comfort when booking flights. According to consumer research, around 21% of travelers now consider physical comfort a deciding factor when allocating their holiday budgets. In response to this growing demand, airlines are investing

stories.title: Future Flight Global announces Florida air service
stories.summary: Future Flight Global plans to launch regional air services in Florida using Pilatus PC-12 aircraft, with later plans to incorporate Beta Technologies electric planes. The company, which describes itself as a mobility management company, intends to sell flights on a per-seat basis under FAA Part 380 rules.

stories.title: Airbus identifies Magnifica Air as ACJ220 customer
stories.summary: Airbus has confirmed that Florida-based Magnifica Air is the customer behind an order for 10 ACJ220-300 aircraft. The airline plans to offer a private class service with cabins seating between 45 and 54 passengers. Operations are expected to begin in 2027.

stories.title: Boeing October deliveries total 49 aircraft
stories.summary: Boeing delivered 49 aircraft in October 2026, a decrease from 57 in September. The total included 32 737 MAX jets and 11 787 Dreamliners. While the manufacturer has delivered 524 aircraft during the first ten months of the year, it remains behind Airbus, which delivered 621.

stories.title: Boeing 737 MAX deliveries reach one-year low
stories.summary: Boeing delivered 32 737 MAX aircraft in October, the lowest monthly total since November 2025. The company previously delivered 43 units in September. Executives have stated the planemaker will miss its target of 500 MAX deliveries for the year as it struggles to stabilize production at 47 planes monthly.

stories.summary: Panic erupted aboard a United Airlines flight bound for New Orleans after a passenger claimed he had a bomb and attempted to storm the cockpit, prompting pilots to issue a hijacking alert. The flight, United Airlines 2174, was carrying 46 passengers and six crew members

stories.title: Air France flight makes unauthorized turn at LAX
stories.summary: An Air France flight departing Los Angeles International Airport made an unauthorized turn, entering the path of another aircraft on a parallel runway. The Federal Aviation Administration said air traffic control issued corrective instructions to the flight. The plane was bound for Tahiti. The incident occurred on Saturday.

stories.title: United Airlines flight issues hijack alert after cockpit breach attempt
stories.summary: A United Airlines flight from Newark to New Orleans issued a Level 4 hijacking alert after a passenger claimed to have a bomb and attempted to enter the cockpit. Crew members persuaded the passenger to move to the rear of the aircraft, where he was detained. The flight landed safely.

stories.title: Pembroke Pines aviation business owner indicted for fraud
stories.summary: Alain R. Ruiz, the owner of a Pembroke Pines aviation parts business, faces federal charges for an alleged scheme involving forged military purchase orders and defrauding investors. A grand jury returned a 12-count indictment in September. Ruiz is currently held for the U.S. Marshals Service.

stories.title: American Airlines plane nearly hit by Air France jet after takeoff at LAX
stories.summary: Two passenger jets operated by Air France and American Airlines came dangerously close in the air after departing from Los Angeles International Airport recently. The incident happened at about 12:20 a.m. on Nov. 7 after the Air France aircraft made a turn it had not

stories.title: SeaPort Airlines adds seasonal route to Olympia
stories.summary: SeaPort Airlines will launch a seasonal route between Felts Field and Olympia Regional Airport in January. The service operates on Fridays and Sundays to accommodate lawmakers and lobbyists. CEO Kent Craford said the route ensures travel to the capital will no longer require an entire day.

stories.title: Helicopter makes emergency landing on Bayonne pier
stories.summary: A sightseeing helicopter made an emergency hard landing at a Bayonne marine terminal after the pilot reported engine failure. The 1999 Bell 206L landed on a pier shortly before 9 a.m. Tuesday. Air traffic control communications confirmed the pilot requested a landing spot after the engine went out.

stories.title: Air Force adopts HondaJet for pilot training
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force has begun using the HondaJet BSTAR programme to supplement B-1B Lancer pilot training. The move aims to protect B-1B airframe hours for demanding missions while providing crews with regular flight time. The first training sortie took place on 2 November in Texas.

stories.title: Illinois student earns Ray Aviation scholarship
stories.summary: Annabelle Longmire, 16, is the first recipient of a Ray Aviation scholarship from Experimental Aircraft Association Chapter 83. The award provides up to $12,000 for flight training. Longmire, who first flew in 2023, plans to earn her pilot certification while still in high school.

stories.title: Ryan Aerospace unveils mixed reality training device
stories.summary: Ryan Aerospace has introduced a T-6 Texan II training device that combines a physical cockpit with a Varjo XR-4 mixed reality headset. The system allows military students to operate physical controls within a simulated environment. It will be exhibited at the I/ITSEC 2026 conference in Orlando.

stories.title: Bombardier Safety Standdown marks 30 years
stories.summary: The Bombardier Safety Standdown event is celebrating its 30th year in Wichita. The three-day conference expects nearly 500 on-site attendees and thousands more online. The event, which is free to attend, focuses on aviation safety and is themed Evolution Fueled by Legacy for this year.

stories.title: FlyBy Aviation Academy expands training fleet
stories.summary: FlyBy Aviation Academy has added a Tecnam P2006T to its training fleet in Spain. The academy, which operates facilities in Burgos and Logroño, provides professional pilot training to students from over 115 nationalities. This addition is part of an ongoing aircraft expansion program for 2026.

stories.title: ATP Flight School opens Dayton training center
stories.summary: ATP Flight School is opening a new training center at Dayton International Airport, expanding its network to 87 locations. The school offers a nine-month Airline Career Pilot Program for students with no prior experience. It includes structured career progression through airline-backed tracks.

stories.title: Cape Fear Community College moves aviation program to airport
stories.summary: Cape Fear Community College has relocated its aviation maintenance technician program to a building at Wilmington International Airport. Instructor Jason Justice described the move as being like settling into a new house. The program previously shared space with diesel technicians, but now has its own facility.

stories.title: Air Force pilots begin training in HondaJets
stories.summary: U.S. Air Force bomber pilots are flying 100 hours per year in contractor-owned HondaJet aircraft to supplement combat training. The Bomber Supplemental Trainer for Aircrew Readiness program began on November 2. The full piece regarding this training initiative is available for subscribers.

stories.title: Veterans seek transition into aviation maintenance careers
stories.summary: Veterans leaving military service are increasingly looking toward aviation maintenance as a potential career path. The field requires technical problem-solving and documentation skills similar to military roles. For those with security clearances, the industry offers a way to continue supporting national defense in a civilian capacity.

stories.title: Huntington symposium highlights women in aviation
stories.summary: The 9th Alys Smith Symposium on Women Professionals is taking place this week in Huntington, West Virginia. The event focuses on the achievements of women across various professional fields, with a specific emphasis on their contributions to the aviation industry.

stories.title: Western Michigan University graduate reflects on aviation career
stories.summary: Bryce Harden, a 2012 graduate of the Western Michigan University College of Aviation, credits his professional path to the influence of his family, peers, and instructors. Harden majored in flight science and administration before building his career in the aviation industry.

stories.title: Skyborne places flight instructors with Avelo Airlines
stories.summary: Skyborne Airline Academy has placed two graduates, Chris Waters and Samuel Howerton, with Avelo Airlines. Both pilots completed FAA Part 141 training at the academy's Vero Beach facility before becoming certified flight instructors. The placement follows an established hiring partnership between the training organization and the carrier.

research.title: A Nested Heterogeneous Multiscale Framework for Power System Dynamic Simulation
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Power system dynamics involve multiple timescales, from electromagnetic transients of the network and inverter-based resources to electromechanical oscillations of synchronous generators and quasi-steady-state evolution of the operating point. Simulating these dynamics with a detailed electromagnetic transient. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

This is a transient strong flow that can be readily imposed in the laboratory using commercial strain-controlled (separate motor. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

To reduce this cost, we introduce a simulation-based inference framework in which a triangular. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: An Interline Multiport DC Circuit Breaker with Power Flow Controller
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Currently, the high-voltage multi-terminal DC (MTDC) grids face two major challenges. First, fast rise rate and lack of zero-crossing point in DC-side fault currents render AC circuit breakers inoperable. Second, DC line currents are passively determined. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Balancing Confidentiality and Attack Detectability in Networked Control Systems over Lossy Wireless Channels
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the joint protection of a networked control system (NCS) against eavesdropping and data integrity attacks over a lossy wireless channel. The eavesdropper intercepts the transmitted sensor measurements and control inputs to reconstruct the system. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Bisect-Index-Choose: A Fast and Exact Algorithm for EV Charging under Minimum Charging Rates
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) charging stations are increasingly operated with an aggregate power limit below the sum of their port ratings, and require scheduling algorithms to divide the available power among the connected EVs. Charging standards permit. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Cable construction effects on the lateral forces and wakes of helically stranded cables under oblique inflow
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Helically stranded cables in aerial towing systems experience oblique inflow, but are often modeled as smooth cylinders, neglecting three-dimensional cross-stream coupling and surface texture. We perform large-eddy simulations and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition for a smooth. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
